messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — after the int4 bring-up for model-x on ded-1 we see context divergence around ~6.5k tokens. Prefill looks OK, then generated tokens shift (position off-by-one). Repro below, putting this here before I file a formal bug. :thinking:

matt: can you paste the minimal repro and any logs you have?

anya: sure — minimal curl to Redwood API we used (trimmed):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"model-x-int4","input":"<long_prompt_7k_tokens>","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```

Output snippet (fp16 expected vs int4 actual):
- expected near token 6542: "...agent replied with confidence."
- int4 actual at same position: "...agent replied with confidence ,"  <-- extra comma + downstream tokens drift

Attached logs: runtime traces show kv-write for seq 6539..6545, then a read at 6542 returns stale/corrupted vector (similarity drop ~0.83 -> 0.36).

devon: hypothesis: rotary embedding phase accumulation under quantized kernel is introducing nonlinear rounding error past certain freq / position. It's not a pure off-by-one, it's phase-warp. Could be precomputed rotary frequencies truncated to int16 or a bug in the packed accumulation in the int4 path. Try comparing the freq table between fp16 and int4 runs.

jing: quick A/B I ran on the same machine: fp16 run matches golden. int4 reproduces the comma-and-drift every time after ~6500 tokens. Also tried reducing "ropemaxscale" knob to 0.5 and the repro window shifts earlier/later depending on value — smells like numeric instability in phase multiplication.

ci-bot: [test #482] kv-coherence-smoke on model-x-int4 — FAILED (kv-index-check assertion at 1739994446).

matt: please open a bug with a minimal repro snippet + the runtime KV diffs and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. Also include the fp16/int4 freq tables and a tiny unit that computes phase differences.

anya: filed bug INFER-983: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFER-983 — included curl repro, runtime traces, and a small python repro that computes rotary phase deltas. Will run the devon suggested kernel tweak overnight.

devon: tentative quick patch to try in the quant kernel (pseudocode):
```c
// clamp accumulation to 32-bit and use float accumulate for phase multiply
uint32_t phase_acc = (uint32_t)(pos * freq_table[i]);
float phase = (float)phase_acc / (1u << 16);
// use higher-precision path for critical multiply
out = cosf(phase) * x - sinf(phase) * y;
```
If that reduces wrap-induced truncation we confirm numeric cause.

anya: I'll queue that patch on a local image and run the overnight long-run. Thanks. @matt @devon @jing — any quick checks I missed? :thumbsup:

matt: capture kernel perf counters too (mmul/warp stalls) and attach. If CI reproduces, mark as P1.

anya: will do. saving logs to the ticket. good night team.
